description: BASED clause (a data item addressed via SET ADDRESS/ALLOCATE), ISO §2023:13.18.5 - a COBOL-2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the ANSI X3.23-1985 data description entry (§1985:VI.5.3.2, whose printed format runs `IS character-string BINARY COMPUTATIONAL COMP` ...) offers after the level-number and data-name-1 or FILLER only the REDEFINES, PICTURE, USAGE (BINARY, COMPUTATIONAL, DISPLAY, INDEX, PACKED-DECIMAL), SIGN, OCCURS, SYNCHRONIZED, JUSTIFIED, BLANK WHEN ZERO and VALUE clauses (the Inter-Program Communication module's level-01 entry adds IS EXTERNAL and IS GLOBAL, §1985:X.4.3.1: "a level 01 data description entry within the Working-Storage Section or File Section determines whether the data record and its subordinate data items have local names"), and §2002:F.1 item 6 ("The following reserved words have been added") lists BASED; §2002:13.16.5 adds "The BASED clause defines a based entry" (§2002:13.16.5.3 GR1: "The BASED clause specifies that the subject of the entry is a based entry defining a template that is dynamically associated with storage through an implicit data-address pointer"), with the dynamic storage of §2002:F.2 item 47 ("ALLOCATE and FREE statements are provided for obtaining storage dynamically") and the pointer class of §2002:F.2 item 103 ("A new class of data is introduced, a pointer type which holds data and program addresses in a machine-specific or system-specific way"). §2014:13.18.5 and §2023:13.18.5.1 carry the 2002 sentence unchanged.
